question: When a driver faces a steady circular green indication, what movements are generally permitted and to whom must the driver yield?
model_answer: Direct Answer: A driver facing a steady CIRCULAR GREEN indication may proceed straight through, turn right or left, or make a U-turn, unless the movement is modified by signs, markings, roadway design, separate turn signals, or other traffic control devices. The driver must yield to pedestrians lawfully within an associated crosswalk and to other vehicles lawfully within the intersection; additionally, drivers turning left or making a U-turn to the left must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to constitute an immediate hazard. Standards (mandatory): - "Vehicular traffic facing a CIRCULAR GREEN signal indication is permitted to proceed straight through or turn right or left or make a U-turn movement except as such movement is modified by lane-use signs, turn prohibition signs, lane markings, roadway design, separate turn signal indications, or other traffic control devices." - "Such vehicular traffic, including vehicles turning right or left or making a U-turn movement, shall yield the right-of-way to: (a) Pedestrians lawfully within an associated crosswalk, and (b) Other vehicles lawfully within the intersection." - "In addition, vehicular traffic turning left or making a U-turn movement to the left shall yield the right-of-way to other vehicles approaching from the opposite direction so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard during the time when such turning vehicle is moving across or within the intersection." Options (permitted): - A steady straight-through GREEN ARROW indication may be used instead of a CIRCULAR GREEN indication to discourage wrong-way turns on approaches intersecting a one-way street or an interchange exit ramp, on approaches with unique geometric design prohibiting turns, or on approaches with pre-signals where adjacent lanes are controlled separately. Citations: - Section 4A.03 Standard §1 (p.644) - Section 4F.01 Option §5 (p.682) - Section 4F.02 Support §2 (p.683) - Section 4F.09 Support §2 (p.693)
gold_answer: The driver may generally proceed straight, turn right or left, or make a U-turn unless another control modifies the movement. The driver must yield to pedestrians lawfully in an associated crosswalk, vehicles lawfully in the intersection, and for left/U-turns, opposing vehicles close enough to be an immediate hazard.
